==English== {{wp}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|tăks}}, {{IPA|en|/tæks/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-tax.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-tax.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{homophones|en|tacks}} * {{rhymes|en|æks|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*teh₂g-|id=touch}} From {{inh|en|enm|taxe}}, from {{der|en|frm|taxe}}, from {{der|en|la-med|taxa}}, from {{cog|la|taxō|t=to appraise, value, estimate; (''medieval'') to tax}}. {{doublet|en|task}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|gafol}}, which was also the word for “tribute” and “rent”. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # [[money|Money]] or goods collected by a [[government]] (or an entity to whom the government has delegated this power, e.g. in [[tax farming]]) to fund itself and its services, for example by levying a charge on [[income]], purchases (sales), [[property]] or [[harvest]], other than that money which is collected by the government in exchange for specific [[goods]] (e.g. the purchase of surplus vehicles). #: {{syn|en|impost|tribute|contribution|duty|toll|rate|assessment|exaction|custom|demand|levy}} #: {{ant|en|subsidy}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=Kunzang Choden|title=Chilli and Cheese: Food and Society in Bhutan|page=147 |text=[They paid a] "mushroom '''tax'''" in addition to their regular '''tax''' of butter and meat. They had to give 1 ''dre'' of dried mushrooms annually to the district administrative centres.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2010-12-06|author=Madison Smartt Bell|title=Lavoisier in the Year One: The Birth of a New Science in an Age of Revolution (Great Discoveries)|publisher=W. W. Norton & Company|isbn=9780393341102|page=5 |text=The [General Farm] organization collected a '''tax''' on salt (''gabelle'') and another on alcohol and tobacco (''aide''), along with customs duties (''traites'') and duties on goods entering Paris from elsewhere in France (''entrées''). Evasion of all of these '''taxes''' through smugglign and other fraud was epidemic{{nb...}}}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-05-17 |author=w:George Monbiot|title=Money just makes the rich suffer |volume=188|issue=23|page=19 |magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly |url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/2013/may/06/politics-envy-keenest-rich |passage=In order to grant the rich these pleasures, the social contract is reconfigured. […]  Essential public services are cut so that the rich may pay less '''tax'''. The public realm is privatised, the regulations restraining the ultra-wealthy and the companies they control are abandoned, and Edwardian levels of inequality are almost fetishised.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261011071319/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2013/may/06/politics-envy-keenest-rich|archivedate=11 October 2026}} # A [[charge]] (of money, food, labor, etc) collected by a person, organization, etc; something required (exacted) from someone who is (really or notionally) under the control of the [[taxer]], such as a contribution or service. #* {{RQ:Beaumont Fletcher Comedies and Tragedies|The Queen of Corinth|passage=Flie far from hence
All private '''taxes''', immodest phrases,
What e'r may but shew like vicious.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=2023-11-20|author=Kates Kennery|title=Pet Cook Book First Edition - Dog and Cat fresh food options plus meals|publisher=Kates Kennery |text=Scrambled egg with cheese [...] careful with the cheese here because it is the main reason for Roxie's runs... [but] We pay a lot of cheese '''tax''' in the house [i.e., when we eat cheese, the dog demands to also be given some].}} # {{lb|en|figurative|uncountable}} A [[burdensome]] [[demand]] #: {{ux|en|a {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|taxen}}, from {{der|en|xno|taxer||to impose a tax}}, from {{der|en|la|taxō|taxāre|t=to handle, to censure, to appraise, to compute}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To impose and collect a tax from (a person or company). #: {{ux|en|Some think to '''tax''' the wealthy is the fairest.}} #* {{quote-book|en|title=Formerly known as food|author=Kristin Lawless|year=2018|ISBN=9781250078315|page=251 |passage='''Taxing''' the food and chemical industries, which make billions off our food consumption, could be another way to generate revenue for the program.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To impose and collect a tax on (something). #: {{ux|en|Some think to '''tax''' wealth is destructive of a private sector.}} # {{senseid|en|overdemand}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To make excessive demands on. #: {{ux|en|Do not '''tax''' my patience.}} #* {{RQ:Melville Omoo |passage=The people of the southeasterly clusters—concerning whom, however, but little is known—have a bad name as cannibals; and for that reason their hospitality is seldom '''taxed''' by the mariner.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[accuse]].
